children: , Google's advertising, cloud and AI parent, is preparing to give its AI chips a brutal new test: operating in space. Shares traded at $344.25 at 10.15am ET time on September 25, up approximately 0.55% from Thursday's close. Project Suncatcher's first orbital experiment is scheduled aboard SpaceX's upcoming Transporter-18 mission. The immediate goal is simple: find out whether Google's hardware can take the punishment.

The attraction is abundant sunlight. Google says satellites in low Earth orbit could generate up to eight times more solar power than installations on the ground. Its Trillium chips have already endured proton-beam testing beyond the estimated radiation dose of a five-year mission. But surviving radiation clears only one hurdle. Launch vibrations and cooling without airflow will put the hardware through a different kind of stress test, while future satellite clusters will need precise laser connections to share AI workloads.

For investors, the distance between a successful experiment and a profitable business remains enormous. Launch costs, equipment replacement and reliable communications still have to make economic sense. The valuation graphic adds another reality check: shares sit 35.1% above the $254.81 GF Value estimate, suggesting a thin margin of safety against that benchmark. Space computing could expand Alphabet's options over time. For now, this mission delivers engineering evidence; a commercial payoff still needs proving.

title: Alphabet Moved Higher as TPUs Chase Power Beyond Earth
